summary: Maximum code-length enforcement pass of deflate-style Huffman tree construction. Reads a frequency-tree descriptor and a tree-state block, walks the tree node-index heap to derive each symbol's code length from its parent depth, clamps any length above the maximum and counts the overflow, then redistributes the overflow by moving leaves to shallower depths and recomputes every overlong symbol's length down to the limit while accumulating dynamic and static bit costs. Invoked by sub_5383D0 (HuffmanTreeConstructor).

local_names.a2: Huffman tree descriptor array; [0] frequency-tree base, [1] max symbol index, [2] tree-state block pointer
local_names.v2: tree-state block pointer (a2[2]) exposing static-tree, extra-bits, extra-base and max-length fields
local_names.v4: static-tree table pointer, null when no static tree is in use
local_names.v23: maximum code length limit (read as v2[4])
local_names.v6: overflow counter (symbols whose code length exceeds the limit)

operations.description: Load the Huffman descriptor: tree base v3 = *a2 (field this+0x0), max symbol index v28 = a2[1] (field this+0x4), tree-state block pointer v2 = a2[2] (field this+0x8); then from the tree-state block read static-tree pointer v4 = v2[0], extra-bits pointer v30 = v2[1], extra-base index v29 = v2[2], and maximum code length v23 = v2[4].
Zero the code-length count table: memset(a1 + 2866, 0, 0x20) clears sixteen word counters (one per candidate code length).
Reset the code length of the tree root to 0: tree[ heap[heap_max] ].Len = 0 where heap_max is the dword at a1 + 5194 and the node-index heap array begins at a1 + 2898.
Main-pass guard: run only when heap_max + 1 < 573 (the tree node-capacity bound); otherwise there are no lengths to redistribute and the function falls straight through to the return.
Main pass over heap slots h = heap_max+1 .. 572: walk the node-index array at a1 + 2898 by dword for (573 - (heap_max+1)) iterations, one heap node per iteration.
Compute the candidate code length for node n = heap[h]: bits = tree[tree[n].Dad].Len + 1, reading the parent depth from the 4-byte tree entry and adding one.
Overflow detection: when bits > v23 (maximum code length), increment the overflow counter v6 and clamp bits = v23.
Store the computed code length: tree[n].Len = bits (word at tree base v3 + 4*n + 2).
Leaf test: only symbols with index n <= v28 (max symbol index) enter the cost-accounting block; internal nodes are skipped.
Increment the length histogram: bl_count[bits]++ (word at a1 + 2*bits + 2866).
Resolve the extra bits: xbits = (n >= v29) ? extra_bits[n - v29] : 0 (dword read from v30 + 4*(n - v29)).
Accumulate the dynamic bit cost: opt_len (dword at a1 + 5787) += tree[n].Freq * (xbits + bits).
Accumulate the static bit cost when a static tree exists (v4 non-null): static_len (dword at a1 + 5791) += tree[n].Freq * (static_tree[n].Len + xbits).

Redistribution loop while overflow v6 > 0: scan downward from max_length-1 to find the deepest bit length v7 whose bl_count word is non-zero, decrement bl_count[v7], increment bl_count[v7+1] by 2, decrement bl_count[v23], and subtract 2 from overflow.

Recompute loop over bit lengths from v23 down to 1: for each of the bl_count[bits] symbols, pop node m from the tail of the heap (a1 + 2898, index descending from 573); when m <= v28 and tree[m].Len != bits, add tree[m].Freq * (bits - tree[m].Len) to opt_len (a1 + 5787) and assign tree[m].Len = bits.
Return the residual loop counter v7; the value is a decompiler artifact and the routine is semantically void (the deflate gen_bitlen counterpart returns nothing).
